sentences.text: I have heard arguments addressed by respective counsels of the parties and carefully perused the record including Trial Court Record.
9. The phenomenon of domestic violence is widely prevalent but has remained largely invisible in the public domain.
Where a woman is subjected to cruelty by her husband or her relatives.
The civil law does not however address this phenomenon in its entirety.

It was therefore, proposed to enact a law keeping in view of the rights guaranteed under Article 14, 15 & 21 of the Constitution to provide for a remedy under the civil law which is intended to protect the woman from being victims of domestic violence and to prevalent the occurrence of the domestic violence in the society.

Keeping these objects and reasons in mind to provide for more effective protection of the rights of the woman guaranteed under Constitution who are victims of violence of any kind occurring within the family and for matter connected therewith or incidental thereto, the Bill was presented and the Protection of Woman From Domestic Violence Act, 2005 was passed by the Parliament.

entities.text: Protection of Woman From Domestic Violence Act, 2005
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Thus, it cannot be lost sight of, that the Act has been passed keeping in view the provision under the Constitution and to provide a remedy under the civil law which is intended to protect the woman from domestic violence in the society.

We may also see that where an alternative constructions are possible, the court must give effect to that which will be responsible for the smooth working of the CA No. 09/2024 Aradhana Srivastava Vs. Vivek Virendra Singh Page no. 10 of 13 system for which the statute has been enacted rather than the one which would put hindrances in its way.

entities.text: CA No. 09/2024 Aradhana Srivastava Vs. Vivek Virendra Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If the choice is between two interpretations, the narrower of which would fail to achieve the manifest purpose of the legislation, we should avoid a construction which would reduce the legislation to futility.

10. The Act inter-alia provides for more effective protection or the right of woman guaranteed under the constitution who are victims of the domestic violence of any kind occurring within the shared household.
According to the Act, any harm, injury to health, safety, life, limb or well being or any other act or threatening or coercion etc. by any adult member of the family, constitutes domestic violence.
Further, the act also contemplates that any woman who is or has been in a domestic relationship, if she is subjected to any domestic violence can file a complaint u/sec. 12 of the PWDV Act.

This Act also covers those woman who are or have been in relationship with the abuser where Aradhana Srivastava vs Vivek Virendra Singh on 9 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40890879/

widows, mothers or single woman or living with the abuse, are entitled to legal protection.
11.
Further, there is no prescribed standard for calculating the compensation amount.

Ld. Trial Court vide impugned order, while considering the annual income of complainant and respondent and CA No. 09/2024 Aradhana Srivastava Vs. Vivek Virendra Singh Page no. 11 of 13 other facts and circumstances of this case, has not only directed the respondent no. 1 to continue to pay the educational/ school fee of minor children by depositing the same directly to the school but also directed to pay Rs. 90,000/- for the maintenance of the complainant as well as minor children from the date of filing of the petition i.e. 06.06.2022 till the disposal of the case on merits, to the complainant.

entities.text: Aradhana Srivastava Vs. Vivek Virendra Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The observation of Ld. Trial Court to give the maintenance of Rs. 90,000/- per month to appellant/ complainant, cannot be considered as non-judicious and irrational and the Ld. Trial Court has given reasons for the same in para 15 to 20 and para 23 of the impugned order.

Ld. Trial Court has passed a well reasoned order by considering carefully the evidence on record and also after taking into consideration the material placed on record by both the parties and has meticulously calculated the aforesaid maintenance amount to the complainant only after taking into consideration their income affidavits and other facts and circumstances of this case.

The maintenance ordered vide impugned order, to the complainant, is adequate and has been granted after considering all the facts and circumstances of the present matter to maintain the children and also to give decent living to the children by providing basic necessities.

Further, considering the fact that respondent no. 1 has legal obligation being father of minor children and husband of appellant, I am of the considered opinion that the interim maintenance as ordered by Ld. Trial Court vide impugned order, is legally correct.
CA No. 09/2024 Aradhana Srivastava Vs. Vivek Virendra Singh Page no. 12 of 13 12.

sentences.text: Therefore, in my considered view, the Trial Court has carefully dealt with the contentions raised on behalf of both the parties and I find no infirmity in the order of Ld. Trial Court.
13. Hence, I conclude that Ld. Trial Court had passed the impugned order legally and correctly.
It was not perverse in nature.
That order passed by Ld. Trial Court needs no further interference.
Present Appeal, therefore stands dismissed.
Ordered accordingly.
